newsitem.title: UK: Brazil issues first emerging market parallel bond.
newsitem.headline: Brazil issues first emerging market parallel bond.

text.p: Brazil launched its well-publicised parallel bond on Monday raising around $540 million equivalent -- the first such euro-linked issue for an emerging market borrower.

The parallel bond structure means that the three tranches -- denominated in Austrian schillings, Dutch guilders and French francs -- will be redenominated to the euro after the single European currency is introduced, scheduled for January 1, 1999.

All tranches therefore have the same five-year maturity and pay a 6.625 percent coupon which will be fungible after European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), creating a more easily tradable euro-Eurobond.
Joint lead managers for the transaction are ING Barings, Banque Paribas and Creditanstalt-Bankverein.
The 2.0 billion Austrian schilling ($164.2 million) tranche yields 175 basis points over the Austrian Bund curve.
The 400 million guilder ($206.2 million) tranche yields 173 b.p. over the interpolated February and June 2002 DSL.
The 1.0 billion French franc ($171.4 million) tranche yields 185 b.p. over the OAT curve.
Brazil's long-term currency rating was recently upgraded to BB-minus from B-plus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
Its long-term foreign currency debt is rated B1 with a stable outlook by Moody's Investors Service.
This year a number of borrowers have launched parallel bonds to position themselves with investors ahead of EMU, but so far this has been restricted to European investment-grade borrowers.

At the investor presentation in London last week, central bank foreign affairs director Gustavo Franco said the parallel bond would diversify Brazil's investor base away from the U.S. and pave the way for other borrowers in the country wanting to tap the international bond market.
Franco added Brazil would take advantage of the scarcity of high yielding bonds from good credits.
